# Yavanna

> Yavanna is the Lady of Fruits and the keeper of all growing things.

*Valar — Valier; Giver of Fruits*

## Overview

Yavanna governs plant life and persuaded the other Valar to preserve a life of shepherding for the Earth.

## Identity

- **Title:** Kementári
- **Role:** Growing things, forests, crops and living creatures
- **Spouse / consort:** Aulë
- **Familiar symbols:** Two Trees; corn-sheaf; Entish life
- **Kindred:** Valier

## Names and Etymology

The name **Yavanna** is used throughout Tolkien's published legends for this figure.
Where an alternative name is known, it is preserved here as a secondary epithet rather than treated as a separate character.

## Character and Domain

In the Ainulindalë and Valaquenta, Yavanna is defined less as a mortal-style personage than as a divine power: a will, office and creative theme made visible.
The sphere associated with Yavanna is **Growing things, forests, crops and living creatures**. Tolkien repeatedly presents the Valar through consorts, crafts, music, duties and the shape of their houses.

## Relationship to Middle-earth

The Valar are the Powers of the World who entered Arda after the Music of the Ainur. They oppose Melkor, preserve creation and generally act through delegated powers rather than constant direct rule.

## Selected Quotes

> Yavanna is the Lady of Fruits and the keeper of all growing things.

*The Silmarillion, Valaquenta.*

> The Valar, the Guardians of the World, are called the Powers of the World; they are the greatest of the Ainur who came to Arda.

*The Silmarillion, Valaquenta (condensed).*

> The Music of the Ainur brought Eä into being, and into its vision the Valar entered.

*The Silmarillion, Ainulindalë (condensed).*
